summary: Zarawar Khan specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Yangon circa 1924–1929, including under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1929), and later studied at the University of Dublin circa 1934–1936.

Religious studies scholar Zayn Kassam held multiple roles at Pomona College, including department chair, Associate Dean for DEI, and John Knox McLean Professor of Religious Studies (1995). She also directed the Pacific Basin Institute and served as director of the Institute of Ismaili Studies in 2023.

Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Zeff Bjerken studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed a PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. in 2001. That year, he held a post at the College of Charleston.

Linguist Zellig S. Harris (1909–1992) studied at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1928–1934) and later taught there from circa 1934 to 1979. He also held a post at Columbia University from circa 1974 to 1985.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Zeng Yang studied as a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under supervisor Jinhua Chen.
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1931 to 1934 under Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. After studying at UC Berkeley (~1943–1947), she trained under teachers including Richard Baker, Mel Weitsman, and Joshin Kasai, later serving as co-abbess of the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at Otani University and Hanazono University.
Zenno Ikuno (born 1928) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University. He served as professor at Taisho University, president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014), and director of the Jodo Shu Research Institute (~2004–2007).

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) was a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held posts there (~1902–1938), at University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955), and at Rissho University (~1949–1954).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning a doctorate from Kyoto University. His career included serving as president of Kyoto University (1949–1961), director of Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972), and president of Kacho Junior College (1973).

Zensho Kitagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught at Rissho University, where he served as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026), and also held an affiliation with the Eastern Institute.
Zesho Machida works in Buddhist studies. Machida held posts as betto at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel works in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998), and has served as a professor at the University of Washington since circa 1999.
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and as a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).

Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and served as an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who completed an MA at the University of Munich in 2005 and an MA at Lanzhou University in 2009.
